ambiguities.description: Does the Enrollment relationship (student enrolls in offering) have its own attributes beyond grade, or is grade attached directly to Student+Offering as a fact type? The transcript treats grade as tied to 'student enrolled in offering' but never names the enrollment relationship as an entity. Should Enrollment be objectified with its own identifier, or is it just a ternary/binary fact?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Is 'Students enroll in course offerings' a distinct fact type from 'student receives grade for offering', or are these the same underlying relationship? The transcript doesn't state whether a student can be enrolled without yet having a grade (e.g., mid-semester), implying enrollment and grade-assignment might be temporally separate facts.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.
A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of Student-enrolls-in-Offering is not explicit: can a student enroll in multiple offerings, and can multiple students enroll in one offering (many-to-many assumed but not explicitly confirmed)? Also unclear if there's a minimum/maximum number of offerings a student must enroll in.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Is the maximum capacity on an Offering a stored business rule or does it also imply an enforced constraint on the number of enrolled students? The transcript states the cap exists but doesn't clarify if enrollment count is validated against it.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

ambiguities.description: Are Semester start/end dates and Course title/credit stored as single value type properties, or could they need more structure (e.g., semester date range with validation start<end)? No constraint on start<end was mentioned.

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.
Every course has a title and a credit value.

ambiguities.description: Is 'Instructor teaches Offering' current-state only, or could an offering's instructor change over time (e.g., substitute instructor)? No temporal tracking was discussed.
